title: 2024年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials—such as steel, concrete and plastic—were found to weigh more than all life on Earth. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors.

P2 Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species.

P3 Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably.

P4 Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived(使复活) by green-thumbed(有园艺才能的) social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.

P5 Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from —the means of production, if you will. They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change. Such planting is a small step for humanity—in the right direction.

questions.q: What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph?
options: The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history.
Economic growth benefits people little in the long run.
It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.
It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 问的是首段作者想强 调什么，是段落主旨而非局部细节。

【拆句】What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 是 What 引导的特殊 疑问句，want to emphasise 是一个简单的动词短语，无从句无否定，结构清爽，无陷阱。 46. What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? A) The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history. B) Economic growth benefits people little in the long run. C) It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. D) It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history. 把段落里一个支撑论据 （2020 年的 tipping point）当作主旨，且"in human history"是过度推断——原文只 说人造物质量超过生命这一比较点。 B) 偷换概念 Economic growth benefits people little in the long run. 把原文"对经济或许有利"扭 曲成"经济增长对人没好处"，攻击点从"与自然的连接"偷换到了"经济增长本身"，并把短 期权衡偷换为 in the long run。 C) ✓ 正确 The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. ↔It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. ↔ It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. 预判要的是"削弱与自然的连接是不明智的"，It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. 正好是这一判断的同义表达，且覆盖整段而不偏向某个论据。 D) 过度推断 It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials. 把"人造物总质量超过生 命"这一比较事实，推断成"使用人造物本身就有害"，原文从未否定使用人造物，只是反 对以此取代真实自然。 研究人员关于流行文化发现了什么? A) 它与自然界日益脱节。 B) 它充斥着各种电子游戏角色。 C) 它特别迎合青少年的口味。 D) 它仍然受到20世纪50年代热门歌曲的影响。

questions.q: What did researchers find about popular culture?
options: It is increasingly detached from the natural world.
It is filled with all kinds of video game characters.
It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers.
It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did researchers find about popular culture? 直接问研究者发现了什么客观事实， 属于细节题。

【拆句】What did researchers find about popular culture? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主谓 researchers find，about popular culture 限定 find 的对象，结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. 对于 1950 年代流行歌曲里每三个与自然相关的词，研究人员发现，50 年后只剩下略多于 一个。 47. What did researchers find about popular culture? A) It is increasingly detached from the natural world. B) It is filled with all kinds of video game characters. C) It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers. D) It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. ↔It is increasingly detached from the natural world. Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. ↔ It is increasingly detached from the natural world. 预判要的是"自然内容大量减少"，A 项用 increasingly detached 这一抽象升级精确对 应该数据，所以锁定 A。 B) 偷换概念 It is filled with all kinds of video game characters. 把原文"孩子认识的游戏角色比野 生动物多"偷换成"流行文化里充斥着游戏角色"——研究比较的是孩子的认知，不是流行 文化的内容构成。 C) 无中生有 It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers. 全句"对青少年口味格外有吸引 力"在 P2 中没有任何对应；原文只是提到青少年将能参加自然史考试，并未谈流行文化 对青少年的吸引力。 D) 与原文相反 It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s. 说流行文化仍受 50 年代流行歌曲 影响，但原文用 50 年代和 50 年后的数据对比，恰恰说明这种影响在减弱、自然主题在 流失，方向相反。 作者建议人们做什么? A) 采取措施确保可持续的食物发展。 B) 通过种植权利重新与自然建立联系。 C) 支持议会对抗社会疾病。 D) 用果树和蔬菜植物覆盖公共空间。

questions.q: What does the author propose people do?
options: Take measures to ensure sustainable food development.
Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.
Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases.
Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author propose people do? 问作者具体提议人们做什么，定位到对应主 张句即可作答，属于细节题。

【拆句】What does the author propose people do? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，propose 后 接"people do"是"propose sb do sth"句型省略了 that 与情态的简略问法，相当于问"作者 建议人们做什么"，无陷阱。 48. What does the author propose people do? A) Take measures to ensure sustainable food development. B) Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. C) Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases. D) Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.

【定位】Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably. 矫正这一社会病的一部分举措，是让议会通过一项"种植权"法案，允许任何人把利用不足的 公共空间改造成菜园和果园。其理念在于让人们重新接触土壤——同时可持续地生产粮食。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Take measures to ensure sustainable food development. 把原文末尾"while producing food sustainably"这一附带的从属信息抬升成了核心主张，掩盖了"重新接 触土壤、与自然重连"这一真正的主诉。 B) ✓ 正确 Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law ↔ Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil ↔ Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. 预判要的两层信息——"通过种植权"和"重新接触自然"——B 项用 through 和 reconnect with nature 一并覆盖，所以是答案。 C) 偷换概念 Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases. 把"议会通过法案"偷换成"人 们站在议会一边"，方向完全反过来——原文是作者建议议会行动，不是建议民众站队 议会。 D) 过度推断 Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants. 把原文"allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces"的"利用不足的公共空间"扩展到"所有公共 空间"，并把"允许"扭曲为"全面覆盖"，方式与范围都被放大。 我们从文章中了解到关于蔬菜种植的什么信息? A) 这一切始于1649年的英格兰南部。 B) 它受到美国政府法规的保护。 C) 它长期以来一直被用于增加食物供应和改善城市景观。 D) 随着社交媒体影响力的增加,它已在全球范围内普及。

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting?
options: It all started in 1649 in Southern England.
It is protected by US government regulations.
It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.
It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 问从文章中获取的事实 信息，属于细节题。 49. What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? A) It all started in 1649 in Southern England. B) It is protected by US government regulations. C) It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. D) It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 主干 What do we learn，from the passage 与 about vegetable planting 都是介词短语作状语，前者点出 来源、后者点出话题对象，结构清晰。

【定位】In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived by green-thumbed social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities. 1649 年 4 月，英国南部居民为应对高物价与粮食短缺，在公共土地上种植蔬菜。把种子炸 弹扔到空地以使其变绿的做法在 1970 年代的纽约兴起，并被有园艺天分的社交媒体网红重 新带火，他们无视当地美国法规，向城市里的丑陋角落"开战"。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 It all started in 1649 in Southern England. 把段内一个时间点放大为"全部起源"，原 文只说 1649 年发生过一次，并未说蔬菜种植起源于此。 B) 与原文相反 It is protected by US government regulations. 与原文 defy local US regulations 直 接相反：原文说网红"无视"美国当地法规，选项说"受其保护"。 C) ✓ 正确 locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England ↔It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green ↔ It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. ↔ It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. 预判要的"补食物 + 美化城市"两条线，C 项用 food supply 与 urban landscape 并 列，正好两条都覆盖，所以是答案。 D) 过度推断 It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media. 把原文里"1970 年代纽约 + 美国网红重新带火"扩张为"全球普及"，并把"重振"延伸 为"日益增长的影响力"，超出原文范围。 除了实用功能外,可公开访问的果蔬园还能做什么? A) 提高人们的环保意识。 B) 增加植物物种的多样性。 C) 充当抵御自然灾害的第一道防线。 50. What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? A) Raise people's environmental awareness. B) Add to the great variety of plant species. C) Act as the first defence against natural disasters. D) Enhance people's community spirit. D) 增强人们的社区精神。

questions.q: What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions?
options: Raise people's environmental awareness.
Add to the great variety of plant species.
Act as the first defence against natural disasters.
Enhance people's community spirit.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 问的是除实用功能之外这些菜园还能做什么，是对应原文并列项的细 节题。

【拆句】What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 主干 What can ... gardens do，apart from their practical functions 作状语限定范围，相当于把"实用功能"这一已知项排除出去；其中 publicly accessible 是副词修饰形容词，整体修饰 gardens。

【定位】They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. 它们能化丑为美，把实用与美感融合在一起，并有助于增强一种社区感。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Raise people's environmental awareness. 把"连接食物与产地、对抗物种丧失"偷换 成"提升环保意识"，前者是行为层面的连接和效用，后者是心理认知层面的意识。 B) 无中生有 Add to the great variety of plant species. 说菜园会增加植物物种多样性，原文从未 谈"增加植物物种多样性"这一功能。 C) 偷换概念 Act as the first defence against natural disasters. 把 first defence against species loss and climate change 偷换成"对抗自然灾害"——物种丧失和气候变化不等于"自然 灾害"，并且选项主语 act as 暗示把整个菜园当成防线，与原文 Plants are 也对不上。 D) ✓ 正确 help promote a sense of community ↔Enhance people's community spirit. 预判要的"增强社区感"在原文里有直接对应的 "help promote a sense of community"，D 项把 promote 替换为 enhance、sense of community 替换为 community spirit，是高保真同义替换，可锁定。
